newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian court says labour leader incited riot.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian court says labour leader incited riot.

text.p: Indonesia's Supreme Court has reimposed a four-year jail term on independent labour leader Muchtar Pakpahan after a review of his acquital found he had incited rioting, the Antara news agency said on Wednesday.

The official news agency quoted the Supreme Court's decision of October 25 as saying Pakpahan, head of the unrecognised Indonesian Labour Welfare Union (SBSI), had incited rioting in the North Sumatran city of Medan in 1994.
The decision was handed down by a three-judge panel headed by former Chief Justice Soerjono and which included his successor, Sarwata, and judge Palti Radja Siregar.
One man was killed in the riots, which caused widespread damage in the industrial city. The rioting stemmed from a series of workers' protests over wages and working conditions.

Pakpahan's lawyers and colleagues said on Wednesday they had still not been officially informed of the decision, which was first reported in local newspapers on Tuesday, quoting unidentified sources at the Medan State Court.
The judges said Pakpahan had intentionally caused the disturbances by urging thousands of workers to demand increases in the minimum wage to 7,000 rupiah ($2.99) a day from 3,100 rupiah ($1.32).
Antara said the court had overruled its previous decision of September 29 last year, handed down by outspoken Supreme Court judge Adi Andojo Soetjipto, quashing Pakpahan's conviction.
Andojo said in the decision that Pakpahan was on the island of Java and not in Medan at the time of the rioting and that it was not proven that he was responsible for the riots.

Pakpahan was originally sentenced to three years in prison by a Medan court in November 1994. His sentence was increased to four years by the Medan High Court in January 1995. Pakpahan was freed in May last year by the Supreme Court, which later quashed the conviction in September of that year.

The Jakarta Post newspaper quoted Andojo as saying he disagreed with the review of his decision. "I believe that under the law, only the defendant or his beneficiary has the right to demand a trial review," he said.
The Jakarta Post also quoted Luhut Pangaribuan, a leading member of the Legal Aid Institute (LBH), as saying the Supreme Court's reimposition of Pakpahan's sentence was a "political decision."
Pakapahan is currently in detention. He was arrested in July on separate subversion charges after riots in Jakarta that month. Subversion carries a maximum penalty of death in Indonesia.
The government blamed the July riots, regarded as the worst in the capital in more than 20 years, on the leftist People's Democratic Party (PRD).
Pakpahan was originally arrested as part of a probe into PRD leader Budiman Sudjatmiko, who the government accuses of masterminding the riots.
